cells.tense: You are standing in the middle of what your own steady practice has made.
cells.ask: Do one deliberate repetition of the thing you've gotten good at, at the level you'd once have been proud of, and stop there.
cells.core: You put in the hours, on your own, and what came back is bigger than the hours. The practice did what practice is for, and you're in contact with that — the skill is yours, the ground it opened is yours, and you can feel the difference.\n\nThat's the part worth saying out loud, because completion isn't a stopping point here. It's where the grip loosens. What you built gets handed over to the next piece of work without you having to guard it, and the loose ends do the wrapping up themselves. You finish a session, close the instrument, and the thing settles on its own.
cells.sheetLine: The practice came in, and you're standing in it.
cells.verb: tending something carefully until it comes in abundant
cells.place: the small, steady practice, kept lit by repetition

cells.tense: You will be rehearsing a finish for something that has not been allowed to finish.
cells.ask: Take one piece of what you've learned and put it in front of someone else before you polish it further.
cells.core: Your eyes are on the far end of the road, on a future where this is proven, and you're straining toward it — adding sessions, adding hours, chasing a shape of the thing that hasn't arrived. There's a finished version in your head you keep measuring the present against.\n\nThe discipline that got you the skill is now the thing keeping it unfinished. Held to a picture you haven't reached, nothing counts as ripe. The abundance is already here, but you can't enjoy it because you're aiming past it. What's needed is the one move you can't make alone — let what you're building meet someone else's hands, and see what it actually is.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing for a finish that's already been reached.

cells.tense: You stopped, and the practice did not come along with you into now.
cells.ask: Pick one small habit from how you used to work and do it once this week, before you feel ready.
cells.core: The small, steady light of just doing the thing, over and over, without needing it to be big — that's what's quiet right now. You're here, and the part of you that used to show up to the work the same way, repeating until it became skill, is not in the room. The repetitions aren't happening, and in their place is a watching of the practice from a distance.\n\nThe discipline isn't dead. It's just not being picked back up. What pulls it back is aiming at something you want far more than you ever wanted to get better — and doing one small thing in that direction, today. The aim does the charging; the practice follows it.
cells.sheetLine: The light is still in you. It needs to be aimed.

cells.tense: You are already running the thousands of repetitions while you tell yourself it is just what you do.
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' out loud, once, about one skill you've been treating as if it were just how you are.
cells.core: The steady work is already happening. The repetitions, the early light, the stubborn return — it's all running, and you steer it. But you describe it as just how you are, or just the job, and the one doing the steering takes no credit. That is what unacknowledged looks like: the work running well, and the person who runs it not in the picture.\n\nWhen it's working well, here's the shape of it: you know you're the one keeping the small light lit, and you say so without needing anyone to agree. Saying it isn't boasting — it's picking up the pen that's already been writing. One sentence is enough.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the light lit. Claim it out loud, once.
